difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y formally unramified between spaces over S, any solid diagram against a first order thickening T ⊂ T' of spaces over S admits at most one dotted arrow — the affineness hypothesis in the definition of formally unramified may be dropped. The retained proof is complete in two lines of genuine reduction: cover T' by a surjective etale map U' from a disjoint union of affine schemes (Properties of Spaces, lemma cover-by-union-affines); a morphism T' -> X is determined by its pullback to U' (descent for morphisms of spaces), and on the affine pieces uniqueness is exactly the definition's hypothesis, so the two candidate arrows agree after pullback to U' and agree on T'. Retained author proof at lines 2783-2789.

dedup.scope: Removal of the affineness test hypothesis from formal unramifiedness for spaces.
